questions.stem: The IUPAC name of $\mathrm{CH_3CHClCH_3}$ is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has three carbons, so the parent is propane. The chlorine is on the middle carbon, which is carbon 2 whichever end numbering starts from. The IUPAC name is 2-chloropropane, also called isopropyl chloride in common nomenclature.

optionRationale.2: The chlorine is on the middle carbon, not the end carbon.
optionRationale.3: This is a common name for the 1-chloro isomer, and the compound here has chlorine on carbon 2.
optionRationale.4: Numbering must give the lowest locant, so position 3 is never used in propane.

questions.objective: Name a simple haloalkane

questions.stem: Which of the following is the formula of the refrigerant Freon-12?
questions.explanation: Freon-12 is dichlorodifluoromethane. Freons are chlorofluorocarbons, which are stable, non-toxic and easily liquefied, and so were used as refrigerants. Their release is harmful because they deplete the ozone layer in the stratosphere.

optionRationale.1: This is carbon tetrachloride, which has no fluorine.
optionRationale.2: This is chloroform, which is not a chlorofluorocarbon.
optionRationale.4: This is dichloromethane, used as a solvent.

questions.objective: Recall the formula of Freon-12

questions.stem: Carbon tetrachloride vapour is heavy and does not burn. One of its uses is in
options: use as an anaesthetic in surgical operations
questions.explanation: Carbon tetrachloride vapour is heavy and non-combustible, so it smothers a fire by forming a blanket over it. It was sold in extinguishers under the name pyrene. It is also used for making refrigerants and as a cleaning solvent, though it is toxic.

optionRationale.1: This is a historical use of chloroform, not of carbon tetrachloride.
optionRationale.3: This is the use of iodoform.
optionRationale.4: DDT is made from chlorobenzene and trichloroethanal, not from carbon tetrachloride.

questions.objective: Identify uses of carbon tetrachloride

questions.stem: Which polyhalogen compound is a yellow solid used as an antiseptic?
questions.explanation: Iodoform (CHI$_3$) is a pale yellow crystalline solid with a characteristic smell. It was widely used as an antiseptic for wounds, although its antiseptic action comes from the free iodine it liberates and not from the compound itself.

optionRationale.1: Chloroform is a colourless liquid and its use was as an anaesthetic and solvent.
optionRationale.2: Carbon tetrachloride is a colourless liquid used in fire extinguishers.
optionRationale.3: Dichloromethane is a volatile liquid solvent, not a solid.

questions.objective: Recall properties and uses of iodoform

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most reactive towards nucleophilic substitution under the same conditions?
questions.explanation: The reactivity of alkyl halides in substitution increases in the order R-F < R-Cl < R-Br < R-I. The C-I bond is the longest and weakest, and the iodide ion is a very good leaving group. So methyl iodide reacts the fastest.

optionRationale.1: Chloride is a poorer leaving group than iodide because the C-Cl bond is stronger.
optionRationale.3: Bromide is a good leaving group but a weaker one than iodide.
optionRationale.4: The C-F bond is the strongest of the four, so fluoride is the poorest leaving group.

questions.objective: Compare leaving-group ability of halogens

questions.stem: Bromomethane is heated with silver fluoride. The main product is
questions.explanation: Alkyl fluorides are made by heating alkyl chlorides or bromides with a metallic fluoride such as AgF, Hg$_2$F$_2$, CoF$_2$ or SbF$_3$. This halogen exchange is called the Swarts reaction. The bromine is replaced by fluorine to give CH$_3$F.

optionRationale.1: Silver fluoride does not act as a reducing agent here; it supplies fluoride.
optionRationale.2: Iodomethane forms from NaI in acetone (Finkelstein), not from AgF.
optionRationale.3: The conversion to the alcohol needs aqueous alkali, not silver fluoride.

questions.objective: Recall the Swarts reaction

questions.stem: Bromobenzene is treated with sodium metal in dry ether. The product is
questions.explanation: Aryl halides couple with sodium in dry ether to give diaryl compounds, which is the Fittig reaction. Two phenyl groups join with the loss of NaBr to give biphenyl, C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_5$. With an alkyl halide as well, the mixed product is the Wurtz-Fittig product.

optionRationale.1: Toluene would need a methyl halide in a Wurtz-Fittig reaction.
optionRationale.2: Benzene would result from reduction, not from coupling with sodium.
optionRationale.4: Phenol is formed with aqueous NaOH under drastic conditions, not with sodium.

questions.objective: Recall the Fittig reaction

questions.stem: Bromoethane reacts with silver nitrite to give mainly
questions.explanation: The nitrite ion is an ambident nucleophile that can attack through oxygen or nitrogen. Silver nitrite is covalent, so nitrogen with its lone pair attacks, giving the nitroalkane. Ionic KNO$_2$ attacks through oxygen to give the alkyl nitrite.

optionRationale.2: Ethyl nitrite is the main product with KNO2, which is ionic and attacks through oxygen.
optionRationale.3: Ethanol needs aqueous alkali; nitrite is not an oxygen nucleophile giving the alcohol here.
optionRationale.4: Elimination to ethene requires alcoholic KOH.

questions.objective: Predict products with ambident nucleophiles

questions.stem: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is heated with alcoholic KOH. The major product is
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH brings about dehydrohalogenation, the loss of HBr. By Saytzeff's rule the more highly substituted alkene is the major product, formed by removing a hydrogen from the carbon with fewer hydrogens. That gives the trisubstituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene.

optionRationale.1: This is the minor alkene, less substituted than the major product.
optionRationale.2: This cannot form directly, since the hydrogen is not removed from the adjacent carbons.
optionRationale.4: The alcohol is the substitution product from aqueous KOH, not alcoholic.

questions.objective: Apply Saytzeff's rule

questions.stem: Among the three isomeric dichlorobenzenes, the para isomer has the highest melting point because
options: it has the highest dipole moment of the three
its symmetrical shape packs well in the crystal
it forms the strongest hydrogen bonds
it has the largest molar mass among them
questions.explanation: The three isomers share the same molar mass, so the difference arises from crystal packing. The symmetrical para isomer fits more closely into the crystal lattice, which needs more energy to break down. Hence it has a higher melting point than the ortho and meta isomers.

optionRationale.1: The para isomer has the lowest dipole moment, as the two C-Cl dipoles cancel.
optionRationale.3: Dichlorobenzenes cannot form hydrogen bonds.
optionRationale.4: All three isomers have the same molar mass.

questions.objective: Explain melting-point trends in isomeric haloarenes

questions.stem: Chlorobenzene is heated with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, and the product is then acidified. The final product is
questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene is unreactive because the C-Cl bond has partial double bond character, so drastic conditions are needed. At 623 K and 300 atm, hydroxide replaces chloride to give sodium phenoxide, which on acidification yields phenol. This is the Dow process.

optionRationale.2: No reduction takes place under these conditions.
optionRationale.3: The chlorine is replaced and a chlorophenol is not formed.
optionRationale.4: The aromatic ring is not hydrogenated by NaOH.

questions.objective: Recall the Dow process

questions.stem: Chlorobenzene reacts with $\mathrm{CH_3Cl}$ in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$. The products are mainly
questions.explanation: This is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation. Although the halogen deactivates the ring by its inductive effect, its lone pairs direct the electrophile CH$_3^+$ to the ortho and para positions. The product is a mixture of o- and p-chlorotoluene, with the para isomer in larger amount.

optionRationale.1: Chlorine directs the incoming group to ortho and para positions, not meta.
optionRationale.2: Benzyl chloride would form by chlorination of toluene's side chain, not by this ring alkylation.
optionRationale.3: Friedel-Crafts alkylation adds an alkyl group; it does not remove the chlorine.

questions.objective: Predict products of electrophilic substitution of haloarenes

questions.stem: 4.6 g of ethanol (molar mass 46 g mol$^{-1}$) is converted to bromoethane (molar mass 109 g mol$^{-1}$) with 80 % yield. What mass of bromoethane is obtained?
questions.explanation: Moles of ethanol = 4.6/46 = 0.10 mol, and the reaction gives one mole of bromoethane per mole of ethanol. Theoretical mass = 0.10 x 109 = 10.90 g. At 80 % yield the mass is 10.90 x 0.80 = 8.72 g.

optionRationale.1: This is the mass at 100 % yield; the question states a yield of 80 %.
optionRationale.3: This divides by the yield instead of multiplying, giving more than the theoretical amount.
optionRationale.4: This applies the 80 % yield twice.

questions.objective: Calculate the actual yield of a haloalkane preparation

questions.stem: 1.01 g of an alkyl chloride on Carius estimation gives 2.87 g of AgCl (molar mass 143.5 g mol$^{-1}$). The compound could be
questions.explanation: Mass of Cl = 2.87 x 35.5/143.5 = 0.710 g, so the percentage of Cl = 0.710/1.01 x 100 = 70.3 %. CH$_3$Cl has 35.5/50.5 = 70.3 % Cl, which matches. C$_2$H$_5$Cl gives 55.0 %, C$_3$H$_7$Cl 45.2 % and CH$_2$Cl$_2$ 83.5 %.

optionRationale.2: Its chlorine content is 55.0 %, lower than the 70.3 % found.
optionRationale.3: Its chlorine content is about 45.2 %, far below the experimental value.
optionRationale.4: Its chlorine content is 83.5 %, well above the experimental value.

questions.objective: Identify a haloalkane from halogen analysis

questions.stem: The hydrolysis of tert-butyl bromide in aqueous medium follows the $S_N1$ mechanism. If the concentration of the bromide is doubled and that of $\mathrm{OH^-}$ is tripled, the rate becomes
questions.explanation: In an SN1 reaction the rate-determining step is the ionisation of the substrate to a carbocation, so rate = k[RBr] and the nucleophile does not appear. Doubling [RBr] doubles the rate, and tripling [OH$^-$] has no effect. The rate becomes 2 times.

optionRationale.1: This multiplies both factors, but the rate does not depend on hydroxide in an SN1 reaction.
optionRationale.2: This counts the hydroxide change only, which does not affect the rate.
optionRationale.3: The rate depends on the substrate concentration, which is doubled.

questions.objective: Apply the first order rate law of the SN1 mechanism

questions.stem: The optically active (S)-3-bromo-3-methylhexane is hydrolysed in a highly polar protic medium. The product alcohol is
options: optically active with partial retention only
questions.explanation: A tertiary substrate in a polar protic solvent reacts by the SN1 mechanism. The leaving of bromide gives a planar carbocation, which water attacks from either face with equal probability. Equal amounts of the two enantiomeric alcohols form, so the product is racemic and shows no optical activity.

optionRationale.1: This would indicate complete inversion, which is the pattern of an SN2 reaction.
optionRationale.2: This would indicate retention, which is not expected for a free carbocation.
optionRationale.4: The planar carbocation is attacked from both faces, giving equal amounts of both enantiomers.

questions.objective: Predict stereochemistry of an SN1 reaction

questions.stem: How many stereoisomers does 2,3-dichlorobutane, $\mathrm{CH_3CHClCHClCH_3}$, have?
questions.explanation: There are two chiral carbons, but both carry the same set of substituents, so the molecule has an internal plane of symmetry in one arrangement. The (R,R) and (S,S) forms are a pair of enantiomers, and the (R,S) form is the achiral meso compound. The total is 3, not 4.

optionRationale.2: This counts only one pair of enantiomers and misses the meso form.
optionRationale.3: This applies the 2^n rule, but the molecule is symmetric so it overcounts.
optionRationale.4: The molecule has two stereocentres, so more than one stereoisomer exists.

questions.objective: Count stereoisomers with identical stereocentres

questions.stem: Chloroform is warmed with concentrated nitric acid. The product, used as an insecticide and a tear gas, is
questions.explanation: Chloroform on reaction with concentrated nitric acid is nitrated at the carbon to give nitrochloroform, CCl$_3$NO$_2$, known as chloropicrin. It is used as an insecticide and fumigant and has tear-gas properties. Phosgene forms instead by oxidation by air in sunlight.

optionRationale.1: Phosgene forms by the air oxidation of chloroform in light, not with nitric acid.
optionRationale.2: Carbon tetrachloride is made by chlorination of methane or carbon disulphide.
optionRationale.3: Iodoform needs iodine and alkali with ethanol or a methyl ketone.

questions.objective: Recall chemical properties of chloroform

questions.stem: Direct iodination of benzene with $\mathrm{I_2}$ does not give iodobenzene smoothly unless an oxidising agent such as $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ is present, because
options: iodine is so reactive that polyiodinated products form
the HI formed reduces iodobenzene back to benzene
the reaction needs only an acid catalyst to proceed
benzene is never attacked by any electrophile at all
questions.explanation: Iodination is reversible, since the by-product HI is a strong reducing agent and reduces iodobenzene back to benzene. An oxidising agent such as nitric acid or iodic acid oxidises HI to iodine, which removes it and drives the reaction forward.

optionRationale.1: Iodine is the least reactive halogen toward direct ring substitution.
optionRationale.3: An oxidising agent is required to remove HI, not only to give acidity.
optionRationale.4: Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution readily with strong electrophiles.

questions.objective: Explain the need for an oxidising agent in iodination

questions.stem: A mixture of bromomethane and bromoethane is treated with sodium in dry ether. How many different alkanes are formed?
questions.explanation: In the Wurtz reaction two alkyl groups join. Two methyl groups give ethane, two ethyl groups give butane, and a methyl with an ethyl gives propane. So the mixture contains three alkanes, which is why the Wurtz reaction with two different halides is not preferred for preparing unsymmetrical alkanes.

optionRationale.1: Cross coupling takes place along with the two self-coupling reactions.
optionRationale.2: This misses the mixed product, propane, formed from one of each halide.
optionRationale.4: Only ethane, propane and butane are possible, so a fourth product cannot form.

questions.objective: Predict the products of a mixed Wurtz reaction

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Haloalkanes are only slightly soluble in water.
Reason (R): They cannot form hydrogen bonds with water, and the energy gained by their attraction to water is less than that needed to break the hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: To dissolve a haloalkane, hydrogen bonds between water molecules have to be broken. The haloalkane-water attractions that replace them are weaker, so the process is not favourable and solubility is low. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

optionRationale.2: The reason gives the actual cause of low solubility, so it is the correct explanation.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true; haloalkanes do not form hydrogen bonds with water.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true: haloalkanes are only sparingly soluble.

questions.objective: Explain the low solubility of haloalkanes in water

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution mainly at the ortho and para positions.
Reason (R): The chlorine atom donates electrons to the ring through the inductive effect and so activates the ring.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Chlorine directs ortho and para because its lone pairs enter the ring by the resonance effect, which increases electron density at those positions. Its inductive effect is electron withdrawing, which overall deactivates the ring. The assertion is true but the reason is false.

optionRationale.1: The reason is false: the inductive effect of chlorine is withdrawing, not donating.
optionRationale.2: The reason is false, so it cannot be a true statement of any kind.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true: chlorobenzene gives o- and p-products.

questions.objective: Separate the inductive and resonance effects of halogens

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Alkyl iodides are more reactive than alkyl chlorides in nucleophilic substitution.
Reason (R): Iodine is less electronegative than chlorine.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The key factor is that the C-I bond is longer and weaker than the C-Cl bond, and the iodide ion leaves readily. Iodine is indeed less electronegative than chlorine, so the reason is a true statement, but it does not account for the higher reactivity. Both are true and R is not the explanation.

optionRationale.1: The explanation is the weaker C-I bond and better leaving group, not electronegativity.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true; iodine is less electronegative than chlorine.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true: RI > RBr > RCl in reactivity.

questions.objective: Distinguish true statements from the actual cause

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): For haloalkanes with the same alkyl group the boiling points follow the order R-F > R-Cl > R-Br > R-I.
Reason (R): The van der Waals forces increase with the size and mass of the halogen atom.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The boiling points rise from fluoride to iodide, R-F < R-Cl < R-Br < R-I, because the larger and more polarisable halogens give stronger van der Waals attractions. The assertion states the reverse order and is false, but the reason is a correct statement of the cause.

optionRationale.1: The assertion states the wrong order, so it is false.
optionRationale.2: The assertion is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true: heavier and larger halogens raise van der Waals forces.

questions.objective: Recall the trend in boiling points of haloalkanes

questions.stem: Match the reaction conditions in List-I with the major organic product in List-II.
questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene gives phenol by the Dow process (A-III). Chloroform with nitric acid gives chloropicrin, CCl$_3$NO$_2$ (B-I). Alcoholic KOH removes HX from chloroethane to give ethene (C-II). Aqueous KOH substitutes the halogen to give ethanol (D-IV).

optionRationale.1: This swaps the matches of B and C: B is actually I and C is actually II.
optionRationale.3: This swaps the matches of A and B: A is actually III and B is actually I.
optionRationale.4: This swaps the matches of B and D: B is actually I and D is actually IV.

questions.explanation: The straight-chain 1-chlorobutane has a larger surface area and a higher boiling point than the branched isomer (A-IV). The symmetrical para isomer packs better and melts higher (B-I). Iodine is far heavier than chlorine, so CH$_3$I is denser (C-II). The C-F bond is the shortest, because fluorine is the smallest halogen (D-III).

optionRationale.1: This swaps the matches of B and D: B is actually I and D is actually III.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the $S_N1$ mechanism.
A. The rate depends only on the concentration of the substrate.
B. A carbocation is formed as an intermediate.
C. Tertiary halides react faster than primary halides.
D. The reaction always gives complete inversion of configuration.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: In SN1 the slow step is the ionisation of the substrate, so the rate depends on the substrate alone (A true), and a carbocation intermediate forms (B true). Tertiary carbocations are the most stable, so tertiary halides react fastest (C true). Attack of the planar carbocation from both faces gives racemisation, not complete inversion (D false).

optionRationale.1: Statement D is false; SN1 gives a mixture of retention and inversion, mostly racemic.
optionRationale.2: D is false, and A and C are also correct.
optionRationale.3: Statement C is also correct, as tertiary carbocations are the most stable.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on the SN1 mechanism

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about haloarenes.
A. The C-Cl bond in chlorobenzene is shorter than the C-Cl bond in chloroethane.
B. Chlorine is a meta-directing group in electrophilic substitution.
C. An electron-withdrawing nitro group at the ortho or para position makes nucleophilic substitution of the halogen easier.
D. Halogens deactivate the benzene ring yet direct the electrophile to the ortho and para positions.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The carbon in chlorobenzene is sp2 hybridised and the C-Cl bond has partial double bond character through resonance, so it is shorter (A true). Halogens are ortho-para directors, so B is false. Electron-withdrawing groups at o- and p-positions stabilise the intermediate for nucleophilic substitution (C true). The halogen deactivates by induction but directs by resonance (D true).

optionRationale.1: Statement B is false; halogens are ortho and para directing.
optionRationale.2: B is false and A and C are also correct.
optionRationale.3: This omits statement C, which is also correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on the reactivity of haloarenes

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about polyhalogen compounds.
A. Iodoform is a yellow solid used as an antiseptic.
B. DDT is not easily degraded in the environment.
C. Chloroform is best stored in transparent bottles in bright light.
D. Freons are stable, non-toxic and easily liquefied gases.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Iodoform is a pale yellow solid with antiseptic use (A true). DDT resists degradation and accumulates in fatty tissues, which is why it is banned in many places (B true). Chloroform is oxidised to poisonous phosgene by air in light, so it is stored in dark, filled bottles; C is false. Freons are stable, non-toxic and liquefiable (D true).

optionRationale.1: Statement C is false; chloroform is kept in dark bottles filled to the brim to prevent its oxidation to phosgene.
optionRationale.3: C is false and A is also correct.
optionRationale.4: C is false, and B and D are also correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on polyhalogen compounds
